defects.what: rationale and observed_substrate_signals misdescribe the verse's own disclosed ketiv/qere note as a SEPARATE rhetorical device: 'a doubled form (an infinitive-plus-finite construction) that intensifies the repayment.' The verse's closing sequence (unpointed word immediately followed by a pointed word, same root) is the standard OSHB encoding of a ketiv (unpointed, Qal 'he will return') immediately followed by its qere (pointed, Hiphil 'he will restore/repay') -- i.e. it IS the chapter's one K/Q note the row itself discloses elsewhere in the same row, not a second, independent literary device. Neither word is even morphologically an infinitive (both are finite imperfect verb forms, Qal vs Hiphil), so 'infinitive-plus-finite' misidentifies the grammar on its own terms independent of the K/Q question. SECONDARY, LOWER-CONFIDENCE NOTE on the same row: the phrase 'the range's one ketiv/qere note falling in chapter 12' is ambiguous -- read with 'range' meaning anything wider than chapter 12 itself (the writer's own p06 part, Prov.12.1-14.35, actually carries 3 K/Q notes; the C2 collection Prov.10.1-22.16 carries 27), the sentence would be false. The row's own second phrasing a few lines away ('the chapter's one disclosed ketiv/qere note') is unambiguous and true, so this is flagged only as a wording-clarity nit riding on the same row, not a separate factual error.
defects.evidence: pmarks_Prov.json kq: Prov.12.14 = 1 note (chapter-12 total = 1, matching the row's claim). The unpointed-word-then-pointed-word adjacency pattern at Prov.12.14 was cross-checked against two OTHER confirmed K/Q verses in the same sampled chapters and shows the identical pattern: Prov.22.14 (kq=1) and Prov.28.8 (kq present) both show an unpointed word immediately followed by a pointed word from the same or a related root, confirming this is OSHB's systematic K/Q encoding, not a one-off literary doubling at 12:14. The row's own isolation and unit_type verdict (single_proverb, synthetic not antithetic) is independently re-confirmed correct and unaffected by this error.

defects.what: rationale and device_notes claim 'the lying-verb and its cognate noun object appear on the same B-colon (breathes lies), a same-root doubling used for emphasis.' The B-colon's verb ('breathes/utters,' root p-w-ch) and its object ('lies,' root k-z-b) are two DISTINCT triliteral Hebrew roots -- not cognate. This is the book's standard verb+object idiom for a false witness pouring out lies (the identical non-cognate pairing recurs elsewhere in Proverbs), not a cognate-accusative/same-root doubling construction. The row's antithetic-parallelism classification (truthful witness vs. lying witness) is independently correct and unaffected by this error; only the specific same-root grammatical claim is wrong.
defects.evidence: OSHB Prov.14.5 B-colon (splice from verse_map_oshb.json): the breathing/uttering verb and the lies-noun that follows it were checked letter-by-letter against their consonantal roots -- p-w-ch (breathe/blow/utter) vs k-z-b (lie/deceive) -- and confirmed to share no root consonants; 'cognate' and 'same-root doubling' do not apply to this pairing.

defects.what: LOW severity, disclosure-rigor gap only (digit is accurate). observed_substrate_signals entry 'exact token (second of two ch.17 occurrences)' never names the swept object, violating the standing 'name the swept object FIRST (spelling vs term vs formula vs construction), then count' rule and the briefs' 'digit-bearing sweeps naming object + unit' requirement -- as written the claim is unverifiable by a reader. Reverse-engineered candidates were swept book-wide restricted to chapter 17: the abomination root (1 hit in ch.17), sheneihem/'both of them' (1 hit in ch.17), and the justify-root of the verse itself (1 hit in ch.17) all fail to produce '2 occurrences'; the token that DOES match is Yahweh -- 2 occurrences in chapter 17 (Prov.17.3 and Prov.17.15), with Prov.17.15 correctly the second. So the underlying digit is true once the object is identified, but the row itself never names it.
defects.evidence: Book-wide skeleton sweeps restricted to chapter 17: abomination root -> Prov.17.15 only (1); sheneihem -> Prov.17.15 only (1); the justify-root of Prov.17.15 itself -> Prov.17.15 only (1); Yahweh -> Prov.17.3, Prov.17.15 (2, matching 'second of two'). No other reasonable candidate token produced a 2-hit chapter-17 count with Prov.17.15 as the second occurrence.
